name: Simulated Annealing
miniText: Can accepting temporary deterioration help escape a poor local optimum? NetLogo Simulated Annealing swaps neighboring black and white pixels while minimizing an energy that favors vertical stripes. Kirkpatrick and colleagues [1] introduce annealing as an optimization method, Černý [2] independently develops the thermodynamic approach, and Metropolis and colleagues [3] provide the stochastic acceptance foundation. Temperature controls willingness to accept worse moves, and a cooling schedule gradually restricts exploration. The original model also exposes whether equal-energy changes are accepted. Swapping preserves color counts, so the search occurs within a constrained configuration space rather than all possible images. Cooling too quickly can leave defects or local traps. The simulation illustrates the tradeoff between exploration and stabilization; a low-energy image from one finite run is not a guarantee of a global optimum or a physical material prediction.
